name: Learn a safe shoulder roll
blurb: A diagonal roll across the shoulder blades that turns a fall into a movement. Worth learning purely as insurance for cycling, skating and stairs.
steps: Learn the path: the roll goes diagonally from one hand, across the shoulder blade, to the opposite hip — never over the head or straight up the spine.
Start from kneeling, tucking your chin and rolling slowly, feeling the diagonal line on your back.
Progress to a squat, then a standing start, keeping the roll round rather than flat.
Roll out to your feet rather than stopping on your back.
Add a small forward step, then a low jump, so it works with momentum.
tips: Chin tucked to the opposite shoulder, always. This is what protects the neck.
Landing on the point of the shoulder means the diagonal is wrong; start again from kneeling.
Bruised spine means you rolled over the vertebrae rather than across the shoulder blade.
proof: A smooth roll on both sides, from standing, straight back to your feet, on a hard-ish surface.
